checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gasLimit validation for P2P-relayed transactions identical to local validation?

reachability.notes: An attacker running a malicious P2P peer can relay crafted transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 to poison the receiving node's mempool.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P message handler for incoming transactions (tb-002 edge). 2. Trace the code path from P2P receipt to txpool insertion. 3. Verify that gasLimit > 16777216 triggers rejection at the SAME validation point as local submissions. 4. Check for any conditional logic that differentiates P2P vs local source before gas validation. 5. Attempt to relay a transaction with gasLimit = 16777217 via P2P and confirm rejection. 6. Compare rejection behavior (error codes, logs) with local submission of same transaction.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Trust Boundary: tb-002, Invariant: INV-002, Threat: stride-002

checklist.title: Verify P2P Peer Handler: Does the P2P message handler enforce gasLimit validation before forwarding to txpool?

reachability.notes: An attacker running a malicious P2P peer can relay crafted transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 to poison the receiving node's mempool.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the actor-p2p-peer message processing code. 2. Identify all code paths that accept transaction announcements/broadcasts. 3. Verify gasLimit validation occurs in P2P layer OR is guaranteed to occur in txpool layer. 4. Check for early-return paths that could skip validation. 5. Review any transaction deserialization that might silently truncate large gasLimit values.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Node: actor-p2p-peer, Supporting check for boundary edge tb-002

checklist.title: Verify Txpool Validation: Does txpool reject transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 regardless of submission source?

reachability.notes: An attacker running a malicious P2P peer can relay crafted transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 to poison the receiving node's mempool.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the actor-txpool transaction acceptance logic. 2. Find the gasLimit validation check (should be <= 16777216). 3. Verify the validation is unconditional (no 'isLocal' flag that bypasses it). 4. Check if validation occurs before or after the transaction is added to any internal queue. 5. Verify rejected transactions do not consume persistent storage or memory. 6. Test edge case: gasLimit exactly equal to 16777216 should be accepted.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, Node: actor-txpool, Supporting check for boundary edge tb-002

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can a malicious P2P peer inject a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 into the mempool?

reachability.notes: An attacker running a malicious P2P peer can relay crafted transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 to poison the receiving node's mempool.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up a target node with default configuration. 2. Connect a malicious P2P peer to the target node. 3. Craft a transaction with gasLimit = 20000000 (> 16777216). 4. Relay the crafted transaction via P2P protocol messages. 5. Query the target node's mempool (via RPC or internal inspection). 6. PASS if transaction is NOT in mempool; FAIL if transaction IS in mempool. 7. Repeat with gasLimit values: 16777217, 2^32-1, 2^64-1 to test boundary conditions.
checklist.risk_category: Denial of Service / Invalid Block Construction
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0003, PoC-based falsification test, Bug Bounty Eligible: true

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the per-transaction gasLimit cap of 16777216 enforced during block validation for P2P-received blocks?

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft and propagate a block via P2P with transactions whose gasLimit exceeds the cap.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the block validation code path for P2P-received blocks (actor-block-validator). 2. Locate the specific check that validates tx.gasLimit <= 16777216 for each transaction in B.transactions. 3. Verify this check occurs BEFORE the block is accepted into the chain. 4. Craft a test block containing a transaction with gasLimit = 16777217 and submit via P2P. 5. Confirm the block is rejected with an appropriate error. 6. Test boundary values: gasLimit = 16777216 (should pass), gasLimit = 16777217 (should fail). 7. Verify the check cannot be bypassed via alternative deserialization paths or encoding tricks.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Invariant: INV-004, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Threat: stride-003. This is the last line of defense for gas cap enforcement at block level. Failure could lead to consensus split if some nodes accept over-cap blocks while others reject them.

checklist.title: Verify P2P Block Reception: Does block deserialization validate transaction gasLimit bounds before passing to validator?

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft and propagate a block via P2P with transactions whose gasLimit exceeds the cap.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the code path from P2P block message receipt (actor-p2p-peer) to block validation. 2. Identify whether transaction gasLimit validation occurs at deserialization layer vs validation layer. 3. Verify no truncation or overflow can occur when deserializing gasLimit values from RLP. 4. Test with malformed RLP encoding that might bypass normal integer parsing. 5. Confirm rejection happens before any state changes or resource allocation. 6. Verify that all transactions in a block are validated, not just sampled.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Node: actor-p2p-peer, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Early validation at deserialization prevents wasted processing on invalid blocks.

checklist.title: Verify Block Validator: Does actor-block-validator iterate ALL transactions to check gasLimit invariant?

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft and propagate a block via P2P with transactions whose gasLimit exceeds the cap.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the actor-block-validator transaction validation loop. 2. Verify the loop iterates over ALL transactions in B.transactions (no early exit). 3. Confirm gasLimit check (tx.gasLimit <= 16777216) is applied to EVERY transaction. 4. Test with a block where only the last transaction violates the cap. 5. Test with a block where only a middle transaction violates the cap. 6. Verify that block rejection is triggered regardless of which transaction violates the invariant.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, Node: actor-block-validator. The invariant requires ALL transactions must satisfy the condition.

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can a malicious P2P peer propagate a block containing a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 that gets accepted?

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft and propagate a block via P2P with transactions whose gasLimit exceeds the cap.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up a target node with default configuration. 2. Connect a malicious P2P peer to the target node. 3. Craft a valid-looking block containing one transaction with gasLimit = 16777217. 4. Propagate the block via P2P protocol. 5. Check if the target node accepts the block (check chain head, logs). 6. PASS if block is REJECTED with clear error; FAIL if block is ACCEPTED. 7. Repeat test cases: (a) single tx with gasLimit = 16777217, (b) multiple valid tx + one invalid, (c) gasLimit = 2^24 exactly (boundary), (d) gasLimit = 2^24 + 1, (e) gasLimit = 2^32 - 1 (max uint32), (f) gasLimit = 2^64 - 1 (max uint64).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0004, PoC: Construct a block containing a transaction with gasLimit = 16777217 and show that a node accepts it. Bug Bounty Eligible: true

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is block validation atomic (all-or-nothing) when any transaction has gasLimit > 16777216?

reachability.notes: Attacker propagates a block with a mix of valid and invalid transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where blocks are received from P2P network and validated. 2. Locate the transaction gas limit validation logic (threshold: 16777216). 3. Verify that when ANY transaction in a block exceeds the gas limit, the ENTIRE block is rejected atomically. 4. Craft a test block containing multiple valid transactions and ONE transaction with gasLimit > 16777216. 5. Submit this block via P2P and verify it is fully rejected (not partially accepted). 6. Check that no transactions from the rejected block are added to the mempool or state. 7. Verify error handling returns appropriate rejection reason. 8. Test edge cases: gasLimit exactly at 16777216 (should pass), gasLimit at 16777217 (should fail entire block).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, Invariant: INV-006, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Critical because partial block acceptance would cause network splits. PoC guidance: Block with one violating transaction among valid ones; show block is fully rejected.

checklist.title: Verify block validator rejects entire block (no partial acceptance) when single transaction violates gasLimit cap

reachability.notes: Attacker propagates a block with a mix of valid and invalid transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the block validator component (actor-block-validator) implementation. 2. Trace the validation flow for each transaction's gasLimit field. 3. Verify that validation fails atomically - no partial state changes occur before full validation completes. 4. Check for any code paths that might accept valid transactions before checking all transactions. 5. Ensure no race conditions exist where valid transactions could be committed before invalid ones are detected. 6. Verify the rejection is deterministic across all nodes (same input always produces same rejection). 7. Test with block position variations: invalid tx at beginning, middle, and end of transaction list.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, Supporting check for actor-block-validator node. Partial acceptance with different transaction sets across nodes directly causes consensus divergence and network split.

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can a block with mixed valid/invalid gasLimit transactions be partially accepted?

reachability.notes: Attacker propagates a block with a mix of valid and invalid transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up two target nodes with default configuration. 2. Craft a block with 5 transactions: 4 valid (gasLimit <= 16777216) and 1 invalid (gasLimit > 16777216). 3. Position the invalid transaction in the middle of the block. 4. Propagate the block to both nodes via P2P. 5. PASS if BOTH nodes fully reject the block AND neither accepts any of the 4 valid transactions. 6. FAIL if either node accepts any transactions from the block OR if nodes have different chain states after receiving the block. 7. Verify by querying: (a) chain head is unchanged, (b) mempool does not contain the valid transactions from the rejected block, (c) state root is unchanged. 8. Repeat with invalid transaction at position 0, 2, and 4 to ensure position-independent rejection.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, PoC: Block with one violating transaction among valid ones; show block is fully rejected. Bug Bounty Eligible: true. This is the definitive falsification test for the atomic rejection invariant.
